newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit holds to range in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit holds to range in quiet session.

text.p: The ringgit kept to a narrow range to track the lacklustre trade in dollar/majors, dealers said.
"Today it was range-trading. The market was not that active," said a dealer at a local bank.
Lack of fresh leads boxed up currencies in Asia.
Another dealer said the ringgit could test higher next week if the dollar reversed direction.
"If dollar/majors market tests lower, we could try 2.4820. If broken, we'll test the 2.48 barrier," he said.
Some dealers said the expected release of December and 1996 Malaysian trade figures next week could help the ringgit due to widespread estimates that the data would show an improving trade balance.
In its market commentary, research house MMS International said there was a market rumour that the December trade would show a deficit of 750 million ringgit.
At 0800 GMT, ringgit was at 2.4828/38 a dollar from 2.4850/60 at the Kuala Lumpur close on Thursday.
